structure: Part 14 read all 18 files of the addresses feature's page and return hand-off in full: page.js, controller.js, template.njk, evaluation.js, parties.js, party-held.js, party-inline.js, party-for-fulfilment-id.js, address-summary.js, same-as-action.js, frozen-parties.js, ins-handshake.js, assert-party-bindings.js, test-support.js, address-return/controller.js, copy/copy.en.js, copy/copy.cy.js and fit/address-return.fit.spec.js. It covers one page, the Consignment addresses page at /live-animals/notifications/{journeyId}/addresses (GET and POST): its caption, heading, intro, fraud warning and maturity banner; five party sections in order (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination) with their headings, hints, add links, Change and Edit details links and inset address; the three same-as copies and their refusals; the conditional CPH number and permanent address sections; and the save actions. It covers the INS address-book hand-off: the add-an-address URL and its four parameters, the per-fulfilment-id handshake token cookie, the fulfilment-id map over the five parties, and the GET-only /address-return route with its landings (select, return, cancel, bare back), its 400 refusals, its not-found and unavailable outcomes, and the one-shot added-address banner the one fit test proves. Since the earlier extract the party list lost its per-party return page and the contact-address party, so the hand-off maps the five consignment parties only and every selection lands on the addresses page; the address summary lost its stop-at-postcode variant. The picker, the edit form and the picker's copy keys are part 15's; the overview task row, the flow section and shared copy are other parts'.

claims.statement: Pressing a same-as control copies the source party's stored address onto the target party, saves it, and brings the trader back to the consignment addresses page where the target now shows that address.

The copy a same-as control makes is an independent copy: it keeps the name, phone, email and address of the source but drops the address-book record it was picked from, so the two parties are not linked afterwards and the source party is left untouched.
claims.note: mechanism: reshapes one stored party answer into the answer saved for another party, dropping the pickedFromId that ties an answer to its address-book record and shallow-copying the address block.

claims.statement: After a same-as copy the target party is shown like any other chosen party, with its own Change and Edit details links, so the copy can then be changed or edited on its own.

claims.statement: A same-as submission for a pair the page does not offer is refused, logged as 'same-as-pair-not-offered', and the trader is returned to the addresses page with nothing saved.
A same-as submission whose source party has no address is refused, logged as 'same-as-source-empty', and the trader is returned to the addresses page with nothing saved.

A same-as submission for a party that already has an address is refused, logged as 'same-as-target-already-held', and the trader is returned to the addresses page with the existing address left as it was.
claims.note: So a same-as press can never overwrite an address already chosen.

claims.statement: After an address has been added in the INS address book, the consignment addresses page shows a success banner titled 'Success' reading '<the address's name> address added to your address book'.
The added-address banner is shown once only: showing it clears it, so it is gone the next time the page is loaded.
The banner is carried between the address book and the addresses page in a cookie named liveAnimalsAddedAddressBanner.
Returning from the address book having selected an address lands the trader on the Consignment addresses page with the added-address banner naming that address.
claims.note: Proven end to end by the one test in address-return.fit.spec.js, driven with a stub address-book record that holds the CONSIGNOR role.

claims.statement: The added-address banner does not time out: it is still on the page ten seconds after it appeared.
claims.quote:
await page.clock.runFor(10_000)
  await expect(addedBanner).toBeVisible()

claims.quote:
await page.reload()
  await expect(addressesHeading).toBeVisible()
  await expect(addedBanner).toHaveCount(0)

claims.note: Follows from the fit spec locating the banner by the alert role; the banner component itself is the shared layout's, another part's.

claims.quote:
export const issueInsAddAddressUrl = (request, h, notificationId, party) => {  …  return insAddAddressUrl({  …  export const insAddAddressUrl = (params) =>
  buildInsFrontendUrl(`${ADDRESS_BOOK_PATH}/add?${new URLSearchParams(params)}`)  …  addNewAddress: sharedCopy.addressHandshake.addNewAddress,  …  addNewAddress: 'Add a new address',
claims.note: The picker page that renders the link is part 15's; the URL and token are issued here.

claims.statement: The hand-off to the address book carries four things: the journey type 'gbn-ag', the notification's id, the fulfilment id of the party being filled, and a handshake token.
Each hand-off issues a fresh random handshake token, 16 bytes shown as hexadecimal, stored against that fulfilment id in a cookie named liveAnimalsAddressHandshakeTokens.
claims.quote:
const HANDSHAKE_TOKEN_BYTES = 16  …  const token = crypto.randomBytes(HANDSHAKE_TOKEN_BYTES).toString('hex')
  storeHandshakeToken(request, h, fulfilmentId, token)  …  addressHandshakeTokens: 'liveAnimalsAddressHandshakeTokens',
claims.note: Several hand-offs can be open at once: the cookie holds one token per fulfilment id.

claims.statement: No add-an-address hand-off is offered for a party the service cannot name a fulfilment id for.
Only a single-valued answer can take part in the address-book hand-off: a party bound to a repeating answer is refused outright with 'Party fulfilment mapping only supports scalar bindings'.
claims.note: It checks the addresses feature's five bindings only.

claims.statement: The INS address book returns the trader to /live-animals/notifications/{journeyId}/address-return, a page reached by GET only.
claims.note: It is registered with the addresses page's own route options, so it is reached under the same conditions as the page itself.

claims.statement: The return carries four things in its query: fulfilment-id, handshake-token, addressId and landing.
The landing the address book names may be one of three: select, return or cancel.
A return naming a fulfilment id the service does not know is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Unknown fulfilment', and the refusal is logged as 'Address return refused'.
A return naming a landing that is not select, return or cancel is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Unknown landing'.
A return that names a landing other than cancel but no address is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Missing address'.
A return that names no landing at all but does carry an address is treated as a selection.
A return that names neither a landing nor an address — someone simply coming back — takes the trader to that party's address picker, saves nothing and needs no handshake token.
claims.note: The token check comes after this branch, so a bare return is always honoured.

claims.statement: Every other return must carry the handshake token the service issued for that fulfilment id, and one that does not is refused with a 400 Bad Request reading 'Invalid handshake'.
claims.note: Security: this is the check that stops a return being replayed or forged for a party the trader never started a hand-off for. The token is compared against the trader's own cookie, so a return cannot be honoured in someone else's session.

claims.statement: A handshake token is used once: it is forgotten as soon as the return is accepted, and the whole cookie is dropped once no hand-off is outstanding.
A trader who cancels in the address book is returned to the notification overview, and nothing is saved.

An address returned as a selection is read back from the address book, copied onto the party as its answer, and the trader is taken to the Consignment addresses page with the added-address banner naming it.
An address returned with the 'return' landing is read back and the banner is shown, but it is not saved onto the party: the trader is taken to that party's address picker to choose it there.
claims.note: So 'select' means the address book chose the party's address for the trader, and 'return' means it only added the address to the book.

claims.statement: The returned address is read scoped to the organisation on the trader's signed-in session, so a record belonging to another organisation is never returned.
claims.note: Security: the address id comes from the query, so the organisation scope on the read is what keeps the lookup to the trader's own address book.

claims.statement: When the returned address cannot be found in the trader's address book, nothing is saved and the party's address picker is shown again with the message 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.'

When the address book cannot be reached while reading the returned address, nothing is saved and the party's address picker is shown again with the message 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'
claims.note: An error that is not a recoverable backend error is not swallowed: it is raised and handled as a server error.

claims.statement: When the selected address was read but could not be saved onto the party, the trader is sent to that party's address picker with the same address-book-unavailable message, rather than being left thinking the address was saved.
Every honoured return is logged as 'Returned from the address book' with the notification, the party, the landing and the address id.
The handshake error is passed to the party's picker page as a query parameter, and an empty value is left off the URL altogether.
claims.note: mechanism: builds the redirect URL back to a party page, dropping empty query values.

claims.statement: A return from the address book does not carry the trader's trail, so the Back link on the Consignment addresses page they land on falls back to the notification overview.
claims.quote: return h.redirect(pagePath(journeyId, addressesPage.slug))
claims.note: Follows because every redirect in the return handler builds a plain page path with no trail, and the page's Back link is kit.trailBackLink, which falls back to the overview when a request carries no trail (claim repo-frontend-p14-010).

claims.statement: The address book's own return URL is not recorded in this repo: nothing in the addresses feature says how the INS address book is told where to come back to.
claims.note: Looked at the four query parameters the add-address hand-off sends, the url helper it uses, and the whole return handler. The helpers that build view-an-address URLs take an explicit `return` path, but the add-address hand-off sends no return path — the address book must derive the address-return URL from journey-type and notification-id itself.

claims.statement: A test-support helper exists so any page that shows the added-address banner can be held to showing it exactly once, with the banner titled 'Success' and reading 'New Farm address added to your address book' on the first load and nothing on the second.
claims.note: mechanism: a shared assertion over the banner cookie, used by the unit tests of the pages that show the banner. The unit tests themselves are out of the source's scope.

claims.statement: The page itself enforces no validation: a trader can save and continue from it with no party chosen, no CPH number and no permanent address, and sees no error summary or error message on the page.
claims.note: Looked for a validate.js in the addresses feature folder (there is none), for any error-summary or field-error block in the template (there is none), and for any check before the redirect in the page's POST handler (there is none beyond the same-as refusals). The mandatory parties are enforced elsewhere — the task-row status and the check-your-answers refusal, both other parts'.

claims.statement: Add a new address sends the trader to the INS address book's add page, carrying the journey type gbn-ag, the notification id, the fulfilment id of the party being filled and a one-off handshake token.
claims.note: ins-handshake.js belongs to part 14's read; claimed here because the picker is where the control is offered.

claims.statement: The picker's maturity banner is the addresses feature's, which is set to 'detailing'.
claims.note: So neither the picker nor the edit page is a signed-off page.

claims.statement: The page reads the stored answers of the five consignment parties at once, and treats a party as chosen only when its stored answer has a name.
claims.note: mechanism: reads every party answer so the page can show each party and decide which same-as controls apply. The map holds the five consignment parties only; the consignment contact address is not one of them.

claims.statement: The fulfilment id the hand-off sends for a party is the id of the obligation that party's answer fills: 89c0d1e2-f3a4-4b5f-8c0b-8d9e0f1a2b3c for the place of origin, 9ad1e2f3-a4b5-4c60-8d1c-9e0f1a2b3c4d for the consignor, abe2f3a4-b5c6-4d71-8e2d-af0a1b2c3d4e for the consignee, bcf3a4b5-c6d7-4e82-8f3e-ba1b2c3d4e5f for the importer and cd04b5c6-d7e8-4f93-8a4f-cb2c3d4e5f60 for the place of destination.
claims.note: mechanism: builds the two-way map between a party and the fulfilment id the address book is handed, over the addresses feature's five bindings. The id values are the obligation ids in obligations/sections/parties.js, outside this part's read, carried forward from the earlier extract's reading of that file.

claims.statement: Only the five consignment parties can take part in the address-book hand-off: a return naming any other fulfilment id, the consignment contact address's included, is refused as 'Unknown fulfilment'.
claims.note: Follows because the fulfilment map is built from the addresses feature's bindings alone and the party list holds no contact party. Whether the contact page offers a hand-off of its own is another part's.

claims.statement: An address can be summarised into one comma-separated line of its address lines, town or city, county, postcode and country, with any empty part left out.
claims.quote:
const ADDRESS_LINE_PARTS = [
  'addressLine1',
  'addressLine2',
  'addressLine3',
  'townOrCity',
  'county',
  'postcode',
  'country'
]

export const addressSummary = (address = {}) =>
  ADDRESS_LINE_PARTS.map((part) => address[part])
    .filter(Boolean)
    .join(', ')
claims.note: mechanism: summarises one address into a single line. Defined in the addresses feature but not used by the addresses page or the return; its callers are other parts'. There is no longer a variant that stops at the postcode.

claims.statement: A party's picker shows a handshake message only for the error codes 'not-found' and 'unavailable'; any other code shows no message.
claims.note: The picker that calls this is part 15's.

claims.statement: The address-return route is registered with the addresses page's own route options, so it is reachable under the same conditions as the Consignment addresses page.
